label: Supporting Artifact / Not a Source of Truth
title: verification-1 rate limiting

checks.name: the first 5 sign-in attempts from one IP are processed, later ones get 429 with an X-Retry-After of 1..60 whole seconds
while limited, even the correct password is refused (429) for that IP, with a valid X-Retry-After
a different client IP is not affected (per-IP bucket)
rotating a forged left-most X-Forwarded-For value does not escape the limit (hardened bridge + 1 trusted hop)
after a process restart the limit still applies (stored in PostgreSQL) and X-Retry-After is valid and has not grown
two instances share one counter: 3 attempts on A + 3 on B -> the 6th is 429, and instance B reports a valid X-Retry-After
20 parallel attempts across two instances: at most 5 are processed (atomic counting), every 429 carries a valid X-Retry-After
the advertised wait is truthful: ~1.5 s before it elapses the IP is still limited, once it has elapsed both instances process attempts again
node-postgres defaults (int8 as string): the count limit still works, but X-Retry-After is not a usable wait time; it matches "lastRequest" and the window joined as text

detail.note: better-auth 1.7.6 computes lastRequest + window * 1000. With a string lastRequest that is a concatenation, not an addition.

checks.name: memory storage: the counter is lost on restart and is not shared between instances

detail.note: Same limit, same IP. 10 attempts were processed where the DB-backed limiter allows 5.

checks.name: guide bridge, single-value X-Forwarded-For: per-IP limiting works
guide bridge, multi-value or missing X-Forwarded-For: every such client shares ONE bucket

detail.note: Client B and the header-less client are refused because client A used up the shared bucket. With the guide bridge, one client can lock sign-in for everyone behind a proxy that appends to X-Forwarded-For. The hardened bridge passes exactly one IP taken from Fastify trustProxy.
